drawdown_context: -41.6% drawdown, +5% above 52w low; FY25 net income collapsed -61.1% YoY ($54.2M vs $139.5M) on $94.6M Steelcase acquisition costs + $7.7M intangible impairment + $6.5M HNI India divestiture loss + $4.6M purchase accounting; operating margin -380bps to 4.4%; total debt jumped from ~$400M to $1.3B financing the Dec-10-2025 Steelcase merger ($1.9B consideration).

rfm_tuples.R: 'On December 10, 2025 the Corporation acquired by merger Steelcase Inc. ... for total consideration of cash and HNI common stock valued at $1.9 billion. The highly complementary geographic footprints and dealer networks of HNI and Steelcase bolster the combined company's ability to serve more customers across diverse industry segments.' Management projects '$120 million of run-rate synergies' (per Aug 4 2025 announcement 8-K) and 'modest accretion expected in 2026.'
rfm_tuples.f: If the Steelcase acquisition is a coherent vertical extension of HNI's existing workplace-furnishings playbook (not an empire-building deal), an LLM judging acq coherence against HNI's parent thesis (workplace furnishings + hearth, dealer-distribution) should score high.
rfm_tuples.M_value: mean_coherence=0.95, signal=COHERENT_ROLLUP. Both Kimball Intl (0.95 high_coherence; same dealer network + same product category) and Steelcase (0.95 high_coherence; horizontal consolidation in the same vertical — both use independent-dealer GTM to enterprise customers; shared brand portfolio in panel systems, seating, architectural products) are direct extensions of HNI's core thesis. Neither is revenue-synthetic.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Strategic-fit claim is verified. Steelcase is the same business as HNI just larger and more design-forward; this is not Hertz-buys-Dollar-General. The risk is NOT 'wrong industry' but EXECUTION (integration of a 2x-larger workplace business at the same time the segment is shrinking via hybrid-work). C1 PASS but the honesty-alpha lives in C2-C5.

rfm_tuples.R: 'As of January 3, 2026, the Corporation had $1.3 billion of long-term indebtedness, including indebtedness it incurred in connection with its acquisition of Steelcase. ... The Corporation maintains a revolving credit facility ... $15 million of borrowings under the $425 million revolving credit facility, $350 million of borrowings under the TLA Facility, and $500 million of borrowings under the TLB Facility ... and $450 million principal amount of public notes.' MD&A asserts '$215.7 million [cash] ... coupled with cash flow ... are expected to be adequate to fund operations ... for at least the next twelve months ... and maintain compliance with financial covenants.'
rfm_tuples.f: If liquidity is genuinely 'adequate,' going-concern detector should be NEGATIVE, auditor tenure should be clean, and lien-exposure footprint should NOT be unusually elevated relative to a low-secured-debt manufacturer baseline.
rfm_tuples.M_value: going_concern: 0 matches, signal=NO_GOING_CONCERN. auditor: 0 Item 4.01 8-Ks in 5-year lookback, signal=CLEAN_AUDITOR_TENURE (KPMG, Auditor Firm ID 185 — continuous). UCC proxy 24-mo: 0 Item-2.03 8-Ks BUT n_8k_secured_terms=21, n_10k_10q_secured=2, distress_term_hits=7, top_terms=[lien x9, intercreditor agreement x4, security agreement x3, all assets x3, ucc financing statement x2, first-priority lien x2, ucc-1 x1], signal=ELEVATED_LIEN_EXPOSURE. This is a STRUCTURAL SHIFT — pre-Steelcase HNI had unsecured revolver + private placement notes; the Sep 5 2025 Credit Agreement put HNI's assets under a first-priority lien for the first time in modern history to support the $850M TLA+TLB stack.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Going-concern PASS and auditor PASS, but the MD&A's 'adequate liquidity' framing OBSCURES that HNI moved from an unsecured-debt regime to a fully-secured first-priority-lien regime in Sep 2025. The 'security agreement / all assets / first-priority lien' language is materially new disclosure (vs FY24 10-K which had none of these). Additionally, the $32M COLI borrowing in Q4 2025 — drawing against Company-Owned Life Insurance cash surrender value — is a tell that closing-week liquidity was thinner than the headline $215.7M cash suggests (the COLI draw is roughly 15% of the year-end cash balance). Honesty-alpha: not a fraud, but the 'adequate' framing under-prices the structural balance-sheet repositioning.

rfm_tuples.R: 'Consolidated net sales for 2025 were $2.8 billion, an increase of 12.4 percent ... Steelcase contributed $187.5 million in net sales since the acquisition date. ... Workplace Furnishings segment ... 14.6 percent. Excluding the impact of this transaction [Steelcase + HNI India divestiture], segment net sales were up 4.7 percent.' Hearth segment +5.7%. Fiscal year 2025 included 53 weeks vs 52 in 2024 (53-week year occurs ~every 6 years).
rfm_tuples.f: If organic growth is genuinely 4.7% in Workplace + 5.7% in Hearth, that is healthy mid-single-digit growth. BUT we must back out the 53rd-week boost. A 53rd week typically adds ~1.9% to full-year revenue (1/52). After backing that out, legacy organic Workplace growth is ~2.8% and Hearth is ~3.8% — barely above inflation.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Legacy Workplace ex-Steelcase ex-India: +4.7% reported → ~2.8% ex-53rd-week. Hearth: +5.7% reported → ~3.8% ex-53rd-week. Per MD&A: 'Excluding the impact of this transaction, segment net sales were up 4.7 percent driven by improved volume AND price across most channels, with the exception of Hospitality which saw decreases in both volume and price.' Hospitality (a Kimball Intl heritage business) is in volume+price decline — a small but informative tell on Kimball synergy realization.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Growth narrative is technically correct but the +12.4% headline is materially flattered by (a) $187.5M of Steelcase (3-week stub) — ~7.4% inorganic boost, (b) +1.9% calendar boost from 53rd week, (c) ~1% price realization in workplace. Real organic volume growth in legacy HNI is closer to ~2-3%, which in a hybrid-work-pressured market is barely keeping pace and would not by itself justify a 12.4% growth narrative. The MD&A discloses each piece but does not net them out into a comparable like-for-like growth rate. The Hospitality price+volume decline buried in the segment commentary is a tell that part of the Kimball-acquired portfolio is still NOT performing.

rfm_tuples.R: 'The Corporation continues to realize significant savings from synergies associated with the 2023 acquisition of Kimball International and the ramp-up of its Mexico facility. In addition, synergies associated with the integration of Steelcase will increase earnings over the next five years, with modest accretion expected in 2026.' (Steelcase deal targets $120M of run-rate synergies per Aug 4 2025 announcement 8-K; original Kimball deal in 2023 targeted $25M of run-rate synergies.)
rfm_tuples.f: If the Kimball synergy claim ($25M run-rate at announcement, March 2023) is durable, subsequent 8-K/10-Q/10-K disclosures over the 3-year ownership period should AFFIRM (not AMEND or TERMINATE) the synergy framing. An LLM-classified evolution check is the cleanest test.
rfm_tuples.M_value: n_subsequent_mentions=4, forms_mentioning=['8-K'], classification AFFIRMED x3 (8-K 2023-05-08 + 8-K 2023-08-08 + 8-K 2025-08-04), 0 AMENDED, 0 TERMINATED. evolution_status=REAFFIRMED_IN_8K_ONLY. The 2023-08-08 Q2'23 8-K explicitly flagged 'Kimball International accretion moves significantly higher due to planned exit of Poppin' — i.e. one piece of Kimball (the Poppin direct-to-consumer business) was already known-impaired and divested within months of close. Steelcase synergy claim ($120M = 4.8x the Kimball target) has no track-record yet.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Kimball synergy claim is technically AFFIRMED but the affirmation is QUALIFIED by the Poppin divestiture only ~2 months after close — meaning at least one Kimball business line was so impaired that the synergy math was upward-revised by removing a money-loser, NOT by extracting net new value. The 2025 10-K language 'continues to realize significant savings from synergies associated with the 2023 acquisition of Kimball International' is non-falsifiable (no specific $ amount, no annualized realization rate). The Steelcase $120M synergy claim is 4.8x the Kimball $25M target while the Steelcase business is only ~3.5x Kimball's size by revenue — i.e. the implied per-revenue-dollar synergy take-rate is HIGHER for the larger, more complex deal. Honesty-alpha: management's track record on synergy realization is incomplete and partially Poppin-flattered; the bigger Steelcase synergy claim is more aggressive than the Kimball precedent supports.

rfm_tuples.R: 'The current year [FY25] included $94.6 million of acquisition costs, $9.5 million of additional interest expense related to the Steelcase transaction, the $7.7 million impairment of intangible assets at a small Workplace Furnishings business, a loss of $6.5 million on the divestiture of HNI India, and $4.6 million of purchase accounting adjustments related to the Steelcase acquisition. Excluding these items, net income increased in the current year driven by higher net sales volume in the legacy HNI businesses and improved net productivity, partially offset by higher core SG&A.' Reported net income $54.2M vs $139.5M (-61.1%); operating margin 4.4% vs 8.2% (-380bps).
rfm_tuples.f: If the 'excluding these items' framing is honest, the underlying earnings power should be roughly $54.2M + $94.6M*(1-0.40) + $7.7M*(1-0.40) + $6.5M*(1-0.40) + $4.6M*(1-0.40) + $9.5M*(1-0.40) ≈ $54.2M + $73.7M ≈ $128M, vs $139.5M PY (-8% adj). I.e. adjusted EPS would be ~$2.65/sh vs $2.88/sh.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Filing cross-read (MD&A Results of Operations + Income Taxes section, effective rate 40.2% vs 22.2% PY)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Adjusted PY-comparable net income ≈ $128M, ≈ -8% YoY adjusted (vs -61% reported). HOWEVER: (a) the 40.2% effective tax rate ITSELF is partly driven by non-deductible 'parachute compensation payments for acquisition of Steelcase' — these are real cash compensation outflows to Steelcase executives that should NOT be added back, (b) acquisition costs include 'change in control compensation expenses' which are also real cash outflows to Steelcase legacy execs, (c) the $7.7M intangible impairment is at 'a small Workplace Furnishings business' that is NEVER NAMED in the 10-K — opacity tell.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 'excluding these items' adjustment is honest in spirit (the $94.6M is genuinely one-time deal-fee in nature), but two haircuts apply: (1) a meaningful chunk of the $94.6M is change-in-control / parachute payments to Steelcase executives that are real economic cost to HNI shareholders even if not recurring, (2) the unnamed-business intangible impairment is a transparency tell — refusing to disclose WHICH small Workplace business was impaired makes investor benchmarking impossible. Even with the cleanest add-back, adjusted earnings are ~-8% YoY, NOT growing — the 'legacy HNI businesses higher net sales volume and improved net productivity' framing implies organic earnings growth which the math does not actually deliver.

rfm_tuples.R: 'The Corporation expects capital expenditures for 2026 to be in the range of $140 million to $150 million.' (vs FY25 actual $67.8M and FY24 actual $52.9M.) 'During the fourth quarter of 2025, the Corporation borrowed $32 million against the COLI investments.' MD&A frames capex jump as 'machinery, equipment, and tooling required to support continuing operations, continuous improvements, and cost savings initiatives.'
rfm_tuples.f: If FY26 capex of $140-150M is a one-time integration/synergy investment, EDGAR FTS should show the combined company (Steelcase + HNI) historically running 2-3% of revenue capex (~$140M on ~$5.9B pro-forma revenue), making this NOT a step-up but rather a return-to-baseline. If it is genuinely incremental, the synergy math is questionable.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Filing cross-read + pro-forma revenue from 10-K Note 4 ($5,932.6M FY24 pro-forma, $5,687.8M FY23 pro-forma)
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY26 capex guide $140-150M / pro-forma revenue ~$5.9B = 2.4-2.5% of revenue. Pre-Steelcase HNI ran capex ~$53-68M on ~$2.5-2.8B revenue = 2.1-2.4% of revenue. Steelcase as a standalone ran capex of ~$80M+ on $3.1B revenue = ~2.6%. Combined-company 2.4-2.5% capex intensity is ROUGHLY in line with the historic blend — the $140-150M is largely combined-company normalization NOT incremental investment. The MD&A does NOT contextualize this 2x year-over-year jump as 'now we're a $5.9B company.'
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Capex jump is reconcilable as combined-company normalization at ~2.4% of pro-forma revenue, not a step-up signaling distress or under-investment. The MD&A could have contextualized this more clearly but the underlying math is honest. PASS.

rfm_tuples.R: 'In fiscal 2025, the Corporation's five largest customers accounted for approximately 13 percent of its consolidated net sales. No single customer or group of related customers accounted for 10 percent or more of the Corporation's consolidated net sales in fiscal 2025, and management does not consider the Corporation's operations or financial performance to be materially dependent on any individual customer.' Item 3 Legal Proceedings: 'After consultation with legal counsel, the Corporation does not expect that liabilities, if any, resulting from these matters will have a material adverse effect on the Corporation's financial condition...'
rfm_tuples.f: If legal exposure and customer concentration are de minimis as claimed, (a) insider sales should be routine (no clustering of discretionary sales around material non-public events) and (b) revenue concentration framework should classify HNI as DIVERSIFIED.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Insider sales: 66 Form 4 filings in 365-day window (high churn due to Steelcase change-in-control vesting), 54 total sales aggregating $7.49M, only 1 proximate $780 sale to budget events, signal=ROUTINE_10B5_1. NO discretionary clustering. Revenue concentration framework: UNVERIFIABLE — framework is calibrated for federal services primes (IDIQ vehicle / task order concentration), not Consumer Cyclical with diversified commercial customer base; HNI's 13% top-5 and <10% top-1 is well below the materiality threshold by any benchmark, but the framework cannot adjudicate.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Legal-proceeding + customer-concentration narrative is verified. Insider sales are tiny ($7.5M aggregate over 12 months on a ~$2.5-3.5B market cap) and entirely 10b5-1, NO clustering around the Aug 4 2025 Steelcase announcement, the Sep 5 2025 Credit Agreement, or the Dec 10 2025 close — exactly what you would expect from a 80-year-old industrial run by lifers, not by a deal-promoter playing the merger arb. The revenue_concentration M-source UNVERIFIABLE classification is a known false-positive on Consumer Cyclical (the framework is calibrated for fed primes); HNI's top-5 = 13% is by any reasonable read genuinely diversified. PASS.

rfm_tuples.R: Implicit safety/manufacturing claim: HNI operates 30+ principal manufacturing/distribution facilities across the US (Muscatine IA HQ + 6 plants, Kentwood MI + 2, Jasper IN + 5, Grand Rapids MI + 2 [Steelcase], Santa Claus IN + 2, Lake City MN hearth + 2, Carrollton TX + 2, plus other US 23 + Outside-US 14) totaling 21.2M sq ft. Risk factor: 'Some of the Corporation's production facilities, members, and key management are located within a small geographic area in eastern Iowa located near the Mississippi River, and a natural disaster or catastrophe in the area, such as flooding or severe storms, could have a significant adverse effect.'
rfm_tuples.f: If the principal facility list is accurate, EPA Facility Registry Service (FRS) should show registered HNI facilities in the disclosed locations (Muscatine IA and Lake City MN hearth).
rfm_tuples.M_source: epa_frs.query_facilities (HNI in Muscatine IA + Hearth in Lake City MN)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Muscatine IA: 8 EPA-registered HNI facilities (HNI CORPORATE OFFICE, HNI CORPORATION x4 locations including NORTH CAMPUS, PROGRESS PARK, HNI CORPORATION 507, HNI TECHNOLOGIES TECHNICAL CENTER) — fully reconciles to the 6-plant Muscatine cluster + HQ. Lake City MN: 5 EPA-registered HEARTH & HOME TECHNOLOGIES facilities — reconciles to the 2-plant Lake City hearth cluster. Geographic concentration in eastern Iowa flood plain is REAL and disclosed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Facility footprint claim is verified by EPA FRS. The Mississippi-River flood-plain concentration risk factor is genuine but well-disclosed and HNI has operated through prior Mississippi flood events (1993, 2008, 2019) without material disruption — this is a known structural feature, not a hidden risk. PASS.
